subject: Tier harmonization: partial upgrade + sandbox add-on routing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@olivelabs.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@olivelabs.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging questions — sandbox + partial upgrade path

Sara / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a concrete next step so we don’t lose momentum: 

- Olive Labs wants to move some workloads to a higher tier for better throughput but keep a subset of endpoints in the current tier to limit spend.
- The ask was for a short-term sandbox (isolated addon) and a partial tier uplift where only specific routes are served from dedicated capacity.

Question for you (and looping in Hiro who owns routing/pricing): is that a) technically supported today, and b) how would we price a hybrid config (pro-rated for the uplifted routes + sandbox seat)?

I attached the MVP-feature-matrix.xlsx that maps the endpoints you mentioned to our capability tiers — please scan and tell us which routes you want to test in the sandbox.

Next step: if we can price a 6-week pilot with a single sandbox + route uplift, we’d like to put a short mutual action plan together and run a tech workshop next week. Are you available Wed (7/21) or Thu (7/22)?

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: MVP-feature-matrix.xlsx

From: Sara Patel <sara@olivelabs.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 09:45:31 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging questions — sandbox + partial upgrade path

Thanks Ben — Wed 7/21 works for a tech workshop (AM PST).

Tom and I reviewed the matrix; we want the following routes in the sandbox: /inference/large-batch, /search/semantic, and /chat/high-priority.

On pricing, we’re trying to avoid committing to a full tier upgrade immediately — can you propose a limited uplift (25% of our throughput capacity) and a way to revert without penalty if we don’t see 2x latency improvement?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
—Sara
Director, Platform
Olive Labs

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@olivelabs.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@olivelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging questions — sandbox + partial upgrade path

Hi Sara — good summary. Short answers up front: yes, we can do it; and yes, we can price a constrained uplift with revert guardrails. Details below.

1) Technical model
- We support route-level routing: requests for selected endpoints can be tagged to a dedicated pool (sandbox or reserved capacity) while the rest stay on the base tier.
- Sandbox is an isolated tenant on a small dedicated pool (no noisy neighbors) — ideal for the three routes you listed.
- KV/prefix cache will be warm for sandboxed routes if you pre-seed via a synthetic run, which improves latency on day 1.

2) Uplift sizing and routing
- Proposal: allocate 25% of your current average token throughput to the uplifted pool (this aligns with your ask). We’ll set an automated fallback to base tier when the pool is at 70% utilization to avoid overage surprises.

3) Pricing options (two approaches)
A) Fixed short-term uplift: one-time 6-week addon fee equal to 35% of the delta between base and tier price for the uplifted capacity, plus a $2,000 sandbox seat fee (covers isolated infra + monitoring retention). Billed at contract start, refundable as a credit if you keep the uplift for 12 months.
B) Metered pilot: no upfront uplift charge, metered consumption during pilot at dedicated pool rates with a capped monthly ceiling (we recommend $12k/mo cap for predictability). Sandbox seat fee still applies.

4) Revert/cutover policy
- Revert window: you can revert to base tier at any time; if you revert within the first 30 days and chose option A, we’ll provide a partial pro-rate refund (50% of the uplift portion).
- SLA: during the pilot we commit to 99.5% availability on the sandboxed pool and will issue a credit for missed uptime per our standard credit table.

5) Next steps
- Ben: propose a formal mutual action plan and pick Wed AM 7/21 for a 90-min workshop.
- Sara/Tom: confirm sandbox endpoints (you already did) and whether you prefer Fixed or Metered pilot pricing.

Happy to run the workshop agenda — I’ll include an ops checklist (KV warm, load shape, synthetic runner).

Best,
Hiro Tanaka
Head of Product — Serving & Runtime
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposal-diff.pdf

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@olivelabs.com>

Thanks Hiro — that breakdown helps. We prefer option B (Metered pilot with a cap). Agree on Wed 7/21 10:00 AM PST for the workshop.

Two quick asks before the meeting:
- Can you send a one-page summary we can share with procurement that lists the cap, sandbox fee, revert terms, and the credit/refund logic?
- Any standard language we should expect in the SOW around data handling for the sandbox? (We need to pass this to InfoSec early.)

If you can get those over by EOD Tue we’ll route to procurement and InfoSec so they can join the workshop if needed.

—Tom
